stories.headline: OpenAI in talks to hand US government a stake of up to 5%

key_facts.fact: OpenAI has discussed giving the U.S. government a stake of up to 5% in the company, the Financial Times reported on July 2, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has discussed giving the U.S. government a 5% stake, the Financial Times reported on Thursday, as AI firms face...

key_facts.fact: The arrangement would channel equity into a 'Public Wealth Fund' intended to distribute the economic benefits of AI to ordinary Americans, with 5% described as the upper bound of a possible range.
key_facts.excerpt: The Financial Times first reported the arrangement, which would channel equity from the AI giant into a so-called 'Public Wealth Fund' intended to distribute the economic benefits of artificial intelligence to ordinary Americans.

key_facts.fact: The concept centers on a voluntary equity donation rather than a government mandate or forced taxation, with discussions between Sam Altman and Trump administration officials ongoing since early 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The concept centers on a voluntary equity donation rather than a government mandate or forced taxation.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI called in April 2026 for a public wealth fund that would provide 'every citizen—including those not invested in financial markets—with a stake in AI-driven economic growth,' and Anthropic has backed a similar idea.
key_facts.excerpt: In April, OpenAI called for the creation of a public wealth fund that would provide 'every citizen—including those not invested in financial markets—with a stake in AI-driven economic growth.'

stories.headline: White House nears voluntary AI model-release standards deal with OpenAI, Google, Anthropic

key_facts.fact: The U.S. government is in advanced talks with AI companies to create voluntary standards for the release of new models, with an announcement possible as soon as next week, the Financial Times reported on July 1, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. government is in advanced talks with AI companies to create voluntary standards for the release of new models, with an announcement possible as soon as next week, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The standards would set benchmarks for advanced models and release timelines while clarifying who can access them in the United States and abroad.
key_facts.excerpt: The standards would set benchmarks for advanced models and timelines, while clarifying who can access them in the United States and abroad, according to the FT report.

key_facts.fact: Google has been in talks with the government ahead of releasing advanced coding models with more sophisticated capabilities, and was involved in broader industry-standards discussions.
key_facts.excerpt: Google has been in talks with the government ahead of the release of advanced coding models with more sophisticated capabilities, a source told Reuters on Wednesday, adding that the company was also involved in broader discussions on industry standards.

key_facts.fact: The talks follow a June executive order directing agencies to work with leading AI developers to test advanced models before release; OpenAI delayed a full public launch of GPT-5.6 at the government's request, limiting access to vetted partners.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has also faced constraints. Last week, it delayed a full public launch of GPT-5.6 at the U.S. government's request, limiting access to a small group of vetted partners.

stories.headline: Basecamp Research brings EDEN antibiotic and vaccine design models to Anthropic's Claude Science

key_facts.fact: Basecamp Research made its EDEN antibiotic-design and vaccine-target-prediction models available through Anthropic's Claude Science, letting researchers generate and prioritize therapeutic candidates via a conversational interface in minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: Basecamp Research today announced that its antibiotic design and vaccine target prediction EDEN models are now available through Claude, including Claude Science, Anthropic's AI workbench for life sciences research.

key_facts.fact: In lab tests with the University of Pennsylvania's Machine Biology Group, 97 percent of EDEN-generated antibiotic peptides were active against WHO priority pathogens; candidate EDEN-7 showed efficacy in mice with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii comparable to last-line antibiotics.
key_facts.excerpt: Laboratory tests showed that 97 percent of EDEN-generated antibiotic peptides were active against World Health Organisation priority pathogens. One candidate, EDEN-7, demonstrated efficacy in mice infected with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii comparable to existing last-line antibiotics.

key_facts.fact: The models are trained on BaseData, built from over 200 global field expeditions and containing over 10 billion genes, the foundation for the Trillion Gene Atlas project with Anthropic, NVIDIA, PacBio and Ultima Genomics.
key_facts.excerpt: The models are trained on BaseData, the company's extensive biological dataset built from over 200 global field expeditions. This dataset contains over 10 billion genes, forming the foundation for the Trillion Gene Atlas project in partnership with Anthropic, NVIDIA, PacBio, and Ultima Genomics.

key_facts.fact: The functionality is accessible through Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Claude Mobile, Claude Code, Cowork and Claude Science via Anthropic's connectors directory.
key_facts.excerpt: The functionality is accessible through Claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Claude Mobile, Claude Code, Cowork, and Claude Science.

stories.headline: Engram exits stealth with $98M to build a learned memory layer for enterprise AI

key_facts.fact: Engram emerged from stealth with $98M in funding to build a learned memory layer that trains AI models to study an organization's world in advance.
key_facts.excerpt: Engram has emerged from stealth with $98M in funding from General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, and Sequoia Capital, building a learned memory layer that trains AI models to study an organization's world in advance, enabling them to match or outperform frontier models while using up to 100x fewer tokens.

key_facts.fact: The company says its models match or outperform frontier models while using 1–10% of the tokens, and get smarter the more they are used.
key_facts.excerpt: Engram compresses that knowledge into reusable model memory that matches or outperforms frontier models while using 1–10% of the tokens. The AI gets smarter the more you use it, and you own the memories.

key_facts.fact: Investors include General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Factory, Modern, Amplify Partners and Neo, plus angels Assaf Rappaport (Wiz), Andrej Karpathy (OpenAI co-founder) and Pieter Abbeel.
key_facts.excerpt: Engram... has emerged from stealth with $98M in funding from General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Factory, Modern, Amplify Partners, Neo and notable angels and advisors including Assaf Rappaport, co-founder and CEO of Wiz, Andrej Karpathy, co-founder of OpenAI, and Pieter Abbeel.

key_facts.fact: Engram launched with a partnership with Microsoft to test its models within Microsoft 365, including a GPU-capacity commitment across Dapple and Azure.
key_facts.excerpt: Engram enters the market with early commercial traction, anchored by a partnership with Microsoft. The two companies are working together to test Engram's models within Microsoft 365... The partnership also includes a commitment to GPU capacity across Dapple and Azure.

sources.title: Engram Launches with $98M to Build AI That Actually Knows Your Organization

stories.headline: AI model lab Scaled Cognition raises $100M Series A for hallucination-free enterprise AI

key_facts.fact: AI model lab Scaled Cognition raised $100 million in a Series A led by Khosla Ventures to build AI that enterprises can trust, focused on reliability.
key_facts.excerpt: AI model lab Scaled Cognition announced it has raised $100 million in a Series A funding round led by Khosla Ventures. The company is focused on solving one of the biggest challenges in AI today: reliability.

key_facts.fact: The company is already in production with Fortune 500 enterprises across financial services, healthcare, telecom and insurance, where a wrong answer has real consequences.
key_facts.excerpt: Scaled Cognition is building AI that enterprises can trust, and is already in production with Fortune 500 enterprises across financial services, healthcare, telecom, and insurance — where a wrong answer has real consequences.

key_facts.fact: Its flagship model APT aims to deliver human-like conversational fluency while eliminating hallucinations; the company was co-founded by CTO Dan Klein (UC Berkeley AI professor) and CEO Dan Roth, who previously built and sold an early agentic AI company to Microsoft.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's flagship model APT delivers human-like conversational fluency while eliminating hallucinations... Founded by Dan Klein, a UC Berkeley professor of AI, and Dan Roth, who together built and sold one of the first agentic AI companies to Microsoft.

stories.headline: TwelveLabs raises $100M Series B to build 'video superintelligence'

key_facts.fact: TwelveLabs raised $100 million in a Series B round to scale its Video Cognition System, the foundation for what it calls Video Superintelligence, announced July 1, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Now, the artificial intelligence (AI) startup has $100 million in new funding to explore that idea, according to an announcement on its blog Wednesday (July 1).

key_facts.fact: The round was led by NEA and NAVER Ventures, with participation from Amazon, Radical Ventures, Korea Investment Partners, Index Ventures, Quadrille Capital and Red Bull Ventures.
key_facts.excerpt: Twelve Labs' Series B round was led by NEA and NAVER Ventures, with participation from Amazon, alongside Radical Ventures, Korea Investment Partners, Index Ventures, Quadrille Capital and Red Bull Ventures.

key_facts.fact: CEO Jae Lee argues AI is leaving a text-based era and pivoting to video, saying the company's goal is to make every second of video 'addressable, searchable, and usable by agents.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'The richest record of reality is still largely outside the semantic layer that modern AI systems use. We are changing that. Our goal is to make every second of video addressable, searchable, and usable by agents.'
